title: LTS-to-Rolling Release Conversion Kit: customer migration & changelog automation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a reusable customer-facing conversion kit and automated changelog pipeline that helps customers migrate from our LTS channel to the new rolling-release cadence. Kit includes a migration guide, staged email/in-app templates, automated semantic changelog generation, compatibility matrix, and a set of optional migration scripts customers can run to opt into minor-version auto-updates.
background: We are shifting long-term support (LTS) customers toward an opt-in rolling-release model for non-breaking performance and infra improvements. Historically customers received quarterly LTS drops; the rolling model provides faster bug fixes and perf gains but requires clear compat/workflow guidance. Past upgrade comms templates focused on single-version migrations; this kit must support both bulk migrations and gradual opt-ins while preserving SLAs and minimizing surprise changes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Public migration guide published to docs with step-by-step instructions and a compatibility matrix
A2: Three channel-ready message templates (email, in-app banner, support canned reply) that legal and support have approved
A3: Automated semantic changelog pipeline hooked to GitHub tags produces human-readable summaries for runtime-2.0 and above
A4: Two migration helper scripts (dry-run mode + opt-in enable) published to GitHub under redwood-tools with tests
A5: Customer pilot (5 customers) completed with feedback triaged and at least two UX iterations incorporated
message_templates:
Email (enterprise):
Subject: Action recommended — optional rolling-release migration for your Redwood runtime
Body: Hi <Account Owner>, we are introducing an opt-in rolling release for non-breaking runtime updates to deliver faster performance and security fixes. No action is required to remain on LTS. If you'd like to opt into rolling releases or run a compatibility check, follow: <migration link>. For questions, open a support ticket.

---
In-app banner (console):
Title: Try faster updates: opt into rolling releases
Body: Switching to rolling releases provides quicker fixes and performance improvements. Click to preview compatibility and schedule an opt-in.

---
Support canned reply:
Summary: Customer asked about upgrade cadence. Response: Explain LTS vs rolling, link to migration guide, offer to run a compatibility dry-run. Provide troubleshooting checklist and invite pilot enrollment.
migration_steps: Step 1: Run compatibility scanner (dry-run) against your workloads using redwood-tools --compat-check --tag runtime-2.0
Step 2: Review generated compatibility report in console and the changelog summary for relevant routes
Step 3: If blockers detected, open a support ticket and include the compat report (support will work with Engineering)
Step 4: For opting in, run redwood-tools --enable-rolling --customer-id <id> or use the console toggle; opt-in can be scheduled
Step 5: After opt-in, monitor the rollout dashboard for regressions; rollback is available via console (can revert to LTS pin within 30 minutes)
Step 6: Confirm with CS and document any non-standard integrations for future automation improvements
changelog_summary: runtime-2.0 introduces a rolling-release channel and a set of performance-focused micro-updates. Notable changes: improved KV cache eviction for long-context workloads, an updated batching heuristic (may change P95 for small requests), and expanded quantization profiles. No breaking API surface changes for the text-generation REST endpoint, but certain internal model variant names have changed (see name mapping table in docs).
